doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Baton Rouge, first New York trip, the road years
title: Deciding to go to New York; saving $800 at a Florida racetrack club
summary: With a baby, he had to test New York or sell shoes; two football players' club in Florida let them save $800.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You told Patti Jones, “I think Mose thought that once we had a baby, we had to start thinking about how we were going to get to New York for him to determine if he could play for a living.” You had to find out if you could make it in New York or not.
Yes. You said, “either we have to go to New York or I have to sell shoes.”
Was that one of your various jobs?

No. Or HE would have to do it. Which meant there was no way we were just going to New York. I guess in there... Is there something about when you worked at the club that those two football players started, and that’s where we saved $800 to come to New York.
Was that a somewhat rough-and-tumble club?
That was in south Florida, at a racetrack.
It was Jo-Jo D’Agostino and...what was his name...the other big football player from Chicago. Caseres or something like that?

Yes, and he and Jo-Jo... Jo-Jo D’Agostino’s father owned a big restaurant that was real famous, and his father set them up. It was the R.J. Reynolds... There was a big clubhouse and a racetrack where they used to do sulky racing, and it was empty, and they rented it, and they opened a club, and of course it attracted all kinds of women because of these two football players. But they weren’t good at running their business... It was like a little hotel. We had rooms upstairs. We had Alissa then. I would put her to bed, and I would run down, and I would be a waitress for a little while, and then I’d run upstairs, and then I’d run down. We saved $800 in a suitcase under our bed, and when we had $800 we went to New York.
